newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mostly stronger, bar flat gasoline.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mostly stronger, bar flat gasoline.

text.p: European oil swaps were steady to a touch firmer on Tuesday as crude futures retraced a little of recent falls, traders said.
Tight heavy fuel helped push June swaps $1 higher easing July into backwardation. Naphtha was up to $2 a tonne stronger while gasoline held steady.

Brent crude CFDs were broadly steady with the balance of this week unchanged at -62 cents under July Brent while June 16-20 firmed a touch to hover around -42/43 under July compared with -46 cents under on Monday.
June 23-27 was unchanged at -37/38 while June 30-July 4 edged a touch higher at -27/28 from -29/30. Nothing was heard concluded.
Heavy fuel swaps gained $1 a tonne with June valued at about $85.50 as tight physical supplies helped propell wet barge numbers to $86 fob and $87.
A reflection of the prompt tightness was July slipping into backwardation of about $1 below June. August was pegged at flat to June, $85.50.

Gas oil spread cracks were broadly steady close in after weakening yesterday and a touch stronger further out. Dealers said 4Q97 was put around $4.53 from $4.55 while 1Q98 was at $4.55 from $4.45.2Q98 also firmed a touch to $4.00 from $3.90.

Naphtha was about $1.50-2.00 a tonne stronger, taking support from stronger screen crude. Dealers said June was valued around $181.50 with July flat. August was showing a $2 a tonne contango, but nothing was heard done.
Gasoline was unchanged, underlinning its bearish tone in a market of tentative gains, traders said. June was pegged at $189 and July at $184.
